title: Supreme Court Allows Green Crackers in Delhi-NCR for Two Diwali Days Only
excerpt: Certified green crackers may be burst only from 6 to 7 a.m. and 8 to 10 p.m. on November 7 and 8, and the complete firecracker ban returns on November 9.
body:
• The Supreme Court has allowed certified green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8 only, between 6 and 7 a.m. and 8 and 10 p.m. each day.
  • Only crackers certified by CSIR-NEERI may be made, sold or burst; crackers containing barium and joined series crackers (ladis) remain prohibited.
  • No crackers may be burst within 300 metres of hospitals, nursing homes, health centres, old-age homes, educational institutions or notified silence zones.
  • The complete ban on firecrackers returns on November 9, the day after Diwali, which falls on November 8 this year.

Delhi-NCR will get a narrow, tightly timed window for Diwali fireworks this year. A Supreme Court bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale, in an order dated October 29 and made available on Monday, permitted the bursting of certified green firecrackers between 6 and 7 a.m. and 8 and 10 p.m. on November 7 and 8, according to Law Trend. Diwali falls on November 8.

What counts as a green cracker

The permission covers only firecrackers approved by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research-National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (CSIR-NEERI). Manufacturers holding valid CSIR-NEERI certification and Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation (PESO) licences may produce only the approved green crackers listed on the CSIR-NEERI website, and only between November 2 and November 6. Firecrackers containing barium, and those not approved as green crackers, remain prohibited, as do crackers joined in series, known as ladis, and garland-style crackers.

https://x.com/republic/status/2117202600575840378

Sale is as controlled as manufacture. Traders whose licences had been cancelled will have them restored temporarily from November 4 to November 6 to sell approved crackers bought from certified manufacturers. District administrations must designate the specific locations where green crackers can be sold; sales anywhere else, including on online platforms, are prohibited.

Where and when bursting is barred

Even inside the permitted hours, the court created no-cracker zones: no bursting within 300 metres of hospitals, nursing homes, primary and district health centres, old-age homes, educational institutions and notified silence zones. Outside the two daily windows on November 7 and 8, bursting is not permitted at all, and the bench stated plainly that the complete ban imposed earlier will be restored from November 9.

"Needless to state that the complete ban on the firecrackers, as imposed earlier, shall be restored with effect from November 9, 2026."

— Supreme Court bench, in its October 29 order

Why the court stopped short of a total ban

Hearing a long-running petition first filed in 2015 on behalf of three infants seeking a blanket ban on firecracker sale and use in the National Capital Region over air quality, the court said a total ban appeared ideal but that it lacked adequate data to conclude such a ban would solve the problem, Verdictum reported. The bench also noted that the complete ban had facilitated the illegal sale of conventional firecrackers under the guise of green crackers — the abuse its certification, designated-sale and inspection conditions are meant to close.

What happens next

The court directed the Central Pollution Control Board, in consultation with state pollution control boards, to prepare daily air quality reports covering November 2 to 6, the Diwali days of November 7 and 8, and the post-Diwali period from November 9 to 30. For residents, the practical rules are simple: buy only CSIR-NEERI-certified crackers, only from designated sellers between November 4 and 6, and burst them only in the two daily windows on November 7 and 8, away from hospitals, schools and other silence zones.
